To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complex chromosomal mosaic of our patient was generated by a double-strand chromosome break on the paternal chromosome nine, that the two broken sister chromatids underwent different healing mechanisms, and that this coincidental chromosome healing was the result of the interaction of two different repair mechanisms, i.e., telomere capture, and neo-telomerisation.

the complex chromosomal mossaicism in our patient was generated by a double-strand chromosome break on chromosome 9 followed by a breakage-fusion-bridge cycle, which resulted in a dicentric chromosome.

the complex chromosomal mossaicism was generated during embryogenesis, by a double-strand chromosome break followed by healing by telomerase-mediated telomere addition and telomere capture, resulting in a dicentric chromosome and a dicentric chromosome with a telomeric fragment, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterisation of a complex chromosome rearrangment in a girl with mental retardation and dysmorphic features.
the mechanisms of chromosome healing, which is a prerequisite for the structural integrity and stability of chromosomes.
the mechanisms generating complex chromosomal rearrangements and the mechanisms by which broken chromosomes are repaired.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this mosaic was the result of a double break on chromosome 9, followed by mitotic separation of the broken chromatids.
this patient is a mosaic of two cell lines with a deletion 2.5 Mb on 9p, one with a deletion 1.8 Mb and one with a deletion of 1.2 Mb, and an inversion of 9p and translocation of 5p.

the complex chromosome rearrangement in this patient was generated by a double-strand chromosome break on the paternal 9p, followed by a mitotic segregation event and subsequent healing of the broken chromosome by telomere synthesis and telomere capture, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the healing of broken chromosomes is not always mediated by the same mechanism.
the mechanism generating complex chromosome mosaics is a combination of double-strand breakage, mitotic misseparation, telomere capture, and neo-telomerization.
the mechanism for chromosome healing depends on the availability of a telomeric sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism(s) of healing broken chromosomes is not limited to either telomere capture or neo-telomerase-mediated synthesis.
the healing of broken chromosomes can be a complex and multi-step process.
complex chromosomal rearrangements can be generated in a stepwise fashion by the sequential occurrence of several breakage-fusion-bridge cycles.
